decisions.text: type stacked_bar_100: fractions of the total are the message, but the audience objects to pies: a 100 % stacked bar (G1.40, D-39)
scale 0–100 by 20: each total 100 %, its parts in % of it (R7-30, G7.32)
one total, Sales, stacked from its 5 parts

stacking order from the base: Sports cars, Other cars, Pickup trucks, Other trucks, Motorcycles (by group, the largest at the base, each group's parts together in their given order: 07 #10, D-24 (b), G7.31)
each part in one colour and one place in every total: Sports cars (slot 1), Other cars (slot 1, its tint), Pickup trucks (slot 2), Other trucks (slot 2, its tint), Motorcycles (slot 3) (G4.22)
one total: one stack, standing upright (07 §5.4), its parts named beside it: vertical stacked bars
5 values against 6 scale labels: whichever puts fewer numbers on the chart (G2.18): the values labelled directly, the value scale and its gridlines removed, the zero line kept as the baseline
value labels as a set, one magnitude and one number of decimals, the prefix and suffix on each: 18%, 41%, 11%, 20%, 10% (G6.16, G7.4)
each value before its part's name beside the stack: the text grey does not read on the parts' colours at 4.5 : 1 inside them (G7.4, G6.5)
the unit's description on its own line above the plot: “Share of total sales”; the labels carry its prefix, suffix and magnitude

each part named beside the stack, level with the middle of its segment, top to bottom as stacked: Motorcycles, Other trucks, Pickup trucks, Other cars, Sports cars (their values before them) (G5.4, D-31 (c))

source.shows: overlapping categories made disjoint in the data (Other cars = Cars − Sports cars) and stacked by group, the larger group at the base, each group's parts together, its second part in a tint of its first's colour (D-24 (b), G0.14); five values against six scale labels, so the values stand before the names beside the stack and the scale goes (G2.18), the text grey not reading on the colours (G7.4)
